reviewHistory.summary: T251 (way-out ring plus page remeasure token) and T253 (UI-6 caption recipe, iOS hangul-word) are correct and well tested. T252 has a P2: the renderer caps the top inset at 0.4 of the viewport height, but the eyeline band always ends below that, so the shipped frame never starts below the band. findings.message: fitSceneBounds computes yMax = 1 - 2*min(insets.top, height*0.4)/height, so it caps any top inset at 0.4*H. The eyeline band's lower edge is always at least CAPTION_EYELINE (0.42)*H + band/2, so every inset framingTopInset raises becomes exactly 0.4*H, inside the band. The measured band height then never changes the shipped frame; only its >0 gate matters. Reproduced at 390x844 beat 5: live band 313-395, computed inset 408, effective frame top 337.6, which is 58px inside the band. The cluster centre sits at ~527 = (337.6+716)/2, matching the cap, not (408+716)/2 = 562 (review-guide/shots/r-390-beat5-outline.png; the worker's t252-after shots show the same). Beats 4/5/7 pass only because the overview's minDistance keeps the small fixture cluster inside the region. Nothing guards a draw whose bounds fill it, for example a high gist lift on beat 7, and scene sets are random per load. Several things describe a frame the code does not produce: the framingTopInset doc ('the frame starts one gap below the band's lower edge'), the test 'starts a narrow eyeline frame one gap below the caption band', the result outcome, and the UI-18 ledger ('~295px-tall region'; the actual region is ~378px). Required: make the composed frame honour the inset. SceneFraming's only consumer is the demo (UniverseFraming -> DemoUniverseScene), so lifting the top cap for this case needs coordinator scope approval for scene-framing.ts. Add a test that composes framingTopInset with fitSceneBounds at 390x844 and asserts that the fitted bounds' projected top is at or below band bottom + CAPTION_SURFACE_GAP_PX. If the cap stays instead, correct the comments, test name, result and ledger to the effective behaviour (top = 0.4*H once a band is measured), and drop the band measurement that cannot affect the output.

Record this as a limit, not a T252 defect, because no rule exists for it. (1) 844x390: the width is at least SHEET_BREAKPOINT.px (48rem = 768px), so the guide's default room is edge. guideCaptionRoom correctly returns 'edge' and T252 leaves the frame alone, as designed. The scout's overlap is the edge band pushed to mid-screen by clearCaptionObstacles: the time row and the CTA row block the top, and the write control or ring blocks the bottom (scout-fallback D-land844: caption [0,164,844,82] at beat 4, [0,216,844,82] at beat 5). That is an ONB-12 edge-room matter, not the eyeline predicate. (2) Landscape under 768px wide, reproduced at 667x375 beat 4: the predicate correctly returns eyeline, yet the whole cluster sits under the caption (review-guide/shots/r-667-beat4-caption-outline.png). Three causes: the guide's obstacle clearing moved the band from the eyeline (116-198) to 164-246, which the page does not mirror; the 0.4*H cap puts the frame at 150-247; and even an honoured inset (211) leaves only ~36px above the 128px bottom inset. This is not a regression: the base frame (96-247) is covered the same way. Fixing it needs an owner rule for short viewports (compare the parked F16/F17). The current limit names only the give-way to edge, not obstacle displacement or landscape.

viewportHeight comes from window.innerHeight inside a useMemo whose deps track neither viewport size. narrow reads window.innerWidth during render, not the guide's tracked viewport, and stays fresh only because the guide's resize remeasure now re-renders the page. A resize that changes neither the room nor the band height keeps the old height. The 0.4*H cap hides this today. It matters once the P2 fix makes the inset take effect, so derive both from a tracked viewport or the canvas size.

At 667x375 the inset is ceil(157.5+41+12) = 211 against a bottom edge of 375-128 = 247, so the overview is fitted into a ~36px strip. At 740x360 a 3-line band hits the MIN_HALF_SPAN guard (~18px). No rule says what the overview frame does when the room below the eyeline band is too thin (F16/F17 are parked), so this needs a coordinator decision, not a worker guess. Option (1): avoid the regression with a stated fallback, for example keep the existing inset when the region below band + gap would be thinner than a named share of the height, or drop the held inset during reveals. Either way the threshold or trade-off must be named by the coordinator or owner. Option (2): accept it under F16/F17 and state it accurately in T252's limits, with the acceptance recorded: under 768px landscape, reveal moments now show the cluster as specks where the base showed it legibly. review.summary: T250 meets its acceptance. SkySphere's optional facing turns the mesh by facing·spin(t) each frame. I checked this numerically against skySpin's Rodrigues form: the faced anchor lands on −Z within 1.5e-8 rad across counts 1–13 and sky times 0–3600 s, and the reversed order would miss by 0.26 rad. count 0 and out-of-range indices face nothing. count 1 is identity, and no NaN appears. The time source is the same `time` uniform the shader reads, read after the clock's increment in the same frame. The ease is 1−e^(−λΔt), so it does not depend on frame rate. Reduced motion is instant, and nothing allocates per frame. The spin constants keep the shader math identical: same axis, and rate×CLOCK per sky second equals the old rate per clock second. Only Grainient, Grainstorm and Liquid Ether spin and publish one. The worker's pixel diff of the unfaced /design skies has max delta 0. The walkthrough facing reads only skyStops (production weight-descending order) and the authored recall target's mood. The recall prompt still faces the heaviest slice, and the turn happens when the memory is recalled. The poster is untouched, the renderer imports neither ui nor universe, and the page passes UNIVERSE_CAMERA_RIG.glideLambda.focusing. Tests: SkySphere.test 20/20, landing 5 files 58/58, apps/web tsc -b clean. The new tests import exports and read a facts field that the base lacks, so they fail there. My own /about run (desktop, ko, port 1237) reproduced the worker's readings exactly. Centre-half lead: CALM 71% at press 5; LOVE 84%, 76% and 92% at presses 9, 10 and 11; LOVE 90% 45 s later. Only optional findings remain.

findings.message: Every SkySphere now runs a second useFrame callback, including unfaced ones (universe, demo, sign-in, EmptySky, and every /design and mobile bench panel). Unfaced, it is a no-op: skyFacingStep returns 1 before Math.exp, advanceSkyFacing returns false and never touches the quaternion, nothing allocates, and the pixel diff is 0. Still, 'nothing added per frame' is not literally true. Optional: return early when there is no static facing and none is held, so an unfaced sphere does no facing work.

Nothing guards the one-line `skyFacing={facts.skyFacing}` forward, which is part of the contract. The scene prop is optional (`skyFacing?: number`) and the section has no test, so deleting the forward still passes tsc and every test; only the UI-15 shots would catch it. Optional: declare the prop as required `readonly skyFacing: number | undefined`, which matches WalkthroughSceneFacts, so tsc enforces the forward.

Comment accuracy. At :122, 'the rig looks down −Z' is wrong for the universe rig, which enters on an elevated camera (VIS-48). It is the canvas's default staged camera that looks down −Z, and facing assumes a host using it. The test comments at :238 ('What the static facing alone showed…') and :267 ('before the constants were published') narrate the first attempt rather than state what the test pins. Optional rewording.

There are two ledger gaps. (1) The round-1 LOVE/STRESS deferral has a reason but no home. UI-20 requires an SSOT decision or a task, and the only record (spec/review/landing-tutorial-ux-261109.md, after base) says it has none yet. The coordinator owns this, since the task marks it out of scope. (2) Round-2 dim 2 calls press 5 'teal-led' but leaves out the classifier's own whole-frame reading, STRESS 43% / CALM 27% chroma-weighted on desktop. My re-measure of the same frame gives a centre-half CALM 71% and a pixel count of CALM 34% vs STRESS 33%. Teal leads where the facing puts it, but not the whole frame decisively, and the ledger should say so.

This is far less than the base, which re-revealed on every mutation, scroll or size tick, so nothing is required. reviewHistory.summary: T257's layout logic is sound. The caption is visible only when layout matches the key and position, so it never paints at the fallback. Size, scroll and font ticks re-measure in place. Room changes (a modal or marked panel mounting) hide, then re-measure. The new tests fail on the old hook (4/4) and pass now. findings.message: The band carrying visibility is the element with aria-live='polite'. key includes the text, so on every caption change ready turns false in the same commit that inserts the new text. The live region therefore leaves the accessibility tree exactly when its content changes, and it comes back already filled one measure later. A room change does the same with unchanged text. The base kept the live root exposed and hid only the paragraph, so a reveal was a content change inside an exposed live region, the case screen readers announce reliably. A live region that appears together with its content is the case accessibility guidance warns is announced inconsistently across screen readers and browsers. ONB-2 makes the caption the guaranteed channel and ONB-13 makes it a polite live region, yet no test or recorded check covers the announcement. Required: keep the live root exposed and unmoving while the visual band hides. Option 1: a fixed root that never moves and paints nothing, holding aria-live, with the positioned band inside it carrying visibility. Option 2: an always-present visually hidden live copy of the text, with the visual band aria-hidden. Then add a test that the aria-live element is never visibility:hidden while a caption is active and that its text changes in place. If the coordinator prefers to keep this structure, record a screen-reader check instead (VoiceOver+Safari, NVDA+Chrome; one announcement per caption, none while hidden). Coupling: T252's DemoPage measures the band through '[data-sequence-chrome][aria-live]' and reads its offsetHeight for the framing inset (DemoPage.tsx ~471). findings.message: fitSceneBounds computes yMax = 1 - 2*min(insets.top, height*0.4)/height, so it caps any top inset at 0.4*H. The eyeline band's lower edge is always at least CAPTION_EYELINE (0.42)*H + band/2, so every inset framingTopInset raises becomes exactly 0.4*H, inside the band. The measured band height then never changes the shipped frame; only its >0 gate matters. Reproduced at 390x844 beat 5: live band 313-395, computed inset 408, effective frame top 337.6, which is 58px inside the band. The cluster centre sits at ~527 = (337.6+716)/2, matching the cap, not (408+716)/2 = 562 (review-guide/shots/r-390-beat5-outline.png; the worker's t252-after shots show the same). Beats 4/5/7 pass only because the overview's minDistance keeps the small fixture cluster inside the region. Nothing guards a draw whose bounds fill it, for example a high gist lift on beat 7, and scene sets are random per load. Several things describe a frame the code does not produce: the framingTopInset doc ('the frame starts one gap below the band's lower edge'), the test 'starts a narrow eyeline frame one gap below the caption band', the result outcome, and the UI-18 ledger ('~295px-tall region'; the actual region is ~378px). Required: make the composed frame honour the inset. SceneFraming's only consumer is the demo (UniverseFraming -> DemoUniverseScene), so lifting the top cap for this case needs coordinator scope approval for scene-framing.ts. Add a test that composes framingTopInset with fitSceneBounds at 390x844 and asserts that the fitted bounds' projected top is at or below band bottom + CAPTION_SURFACE_GAP_PX. If the cap stays instead, correct the comments, test name, result and ledger to the effective behaviour (top = 0.4*H once a band is measured), and drop the band measurement that cannot affect the output.

Record this as a limit, not a T252 defect, because no rule exists for it. (1) 844x390: the width is at least SHEET_BREAKPOINT.px (48rem = 768px), so the guide's default room is edge. guideCaptionRoom correctly returns 'edge' and T252 leaves the frame alone, as designed. The scout's overlap is the edge band pushed to mid-screen by clearCaptionObstacles: the time row and the CTA row block the top, and the write control or ring blocks the bottom (scout-fallback D-land844: caption [0,164,844,82] at beat 4, [0,216,844,82] at beat 5). That is an ONB-12 edge-room matter, not the eyeline predicate. (2) Landscape under 768px wide, reproduced at 667x375 beat 4: the predicate correctly returns eyeline, yet the whole cluster sits under the caption (review-guide/shots/r-667-beat4-caption-outline.png). Three causes: the guide's obstacle clearing moved the band from the eyeline (116-198) to 164-246, which the page does not mirror; the 0.4*H cap puts the frame at 150-247; and even an honoured inset (211) leaves only ~36px above the 128px bottom inset. This is not a regression: the base frame (96-247) is covered the same way. Fixing it needs an owner rule for short viewports (compare the parked F16/F17). The current limit names only the give-way to edge, not obstacle displacement or landscape.

viewportHeight comes from window.innerHeight inside a useMemo whose deps track neither viewport size. narrow reads window.innerWidth during render, not the guide's tracked viewport, and stays fresh only because the guide's resize remeasure now re-renders the page. A resize that changes neither the room nor the band height keeps the old height. The 0.4*H cap hides this today. It matters once the P2 fix makes the inset take effect, so derive both from a tracked viewport or the canvas size.

review.summary: T250 meets its acceptance. SkySphere's optional facing turns the mesh by facing·spin(t) each frame. I checked this numerically against skySpin's Rodrigues form: the faced anchor lands on −Z within 1.5e-8 rad across counts 1–13 and sky times 0–3600 s, and the reversed order would miss by 0.26 rad. count 0 and out-of-range indices face nothing. count 1 is identity, and no NaN appears. The time source is the same `time` uniform the shader reads, read after the clock's increment in the same frame. The ease is 1−e^(−λΔt), so it does not depend on frame rate. Reduced motion is instant, and nothing allocates per frame. The spin constants keep the shader math identical: same axis, and rate×CLOCK per sky second equals the old rate per clock second. Only Grainient, Grainstorm and Liquid Ether spin and publish one. The worker's pixel diff of the unfaced /design skies has max delta 0. The walkthrough facing reads only skyStops (production weight-descending order) and the authored recall target's mood. The recall prompt still faces the heaviest slice, and the turn happens when the memory is recalled. The poster is untouched, the renderer imports neither ui nor universe, and the page passes UNIVERSE_CAMERA_RIG.glideLambda.focusing. Tests: SkySphere.test 20/20, landing 5 files 58/58, apps/web tsc -b clean. The new tests import exports and read a facts field that the base lacks, so they fail there. My own /about run (desktop, ko, port 1237) reproduced the worker's readings exactly. Centre-half lead: CALM 71% at press 5; LOVE 84%, 76% and 92% at presses 9, 10 and 11; LOVE 90% 45 s later. Only optional findings remain.

findings.message: Every SkySphere now runs a second useFrame callback, including unfaced ones (universe, demo, sign-in, EmptySky, and every /design and mobile bench panel). Unfaced, it is a no-op: skyFacingStep returns 1 before Math.exp, advanceSkyFacing returns false and never touches the quaternion, nothing allocates, and the pixel diff is 0. Still, 'nothing added per frame' is not literally true. Optional: return early when there is no static facing and none is held, so an unfaced sphere does no facing work.

Nothing guards the one-line `skyFacing={facts.skyFacing}` forward, which is part of the contract. The scene prop is optional (`skyFacing?: number`) and the section has no test, so deleting the forward still passes tsc and every test; only the UI-15 shots would catch it. Optional: declare the prop as required `readonly skyFacing: number | undefined`, which matches WalkthroughSceneFacts, so tsc enforces the forward.

Comment accuracy. At :122, 'the rig looks down −Z' is wrong for the universe rig, which enters on an elevated camera (VIS-48). It is the canvas's default staged camera that looks down −Z, and facing assumes a host using it. The test comments at :238 ('What the static facing alone showed…') and :267 ('before the constants were published') narrate the first attempt rather than state what the test pins. Optional rewording.

There are two ledger gaps. (1) The round-1 LOVE/STRESS deferral has a reason but no home. UI-20 requires an SSOT decision or a task, and the only record (spec/review/landing-tutorial-ux-261109.md, after base) says it has none yet. The coordinator owns this, since the task marks it out of scope. (2) Round-2 dim 2 calls press 5 'teal-led' but leaves out the classifier's own whole-frame reading, STRESS 43% / CALM 27% chroma-weighted on desktop. My re-measure of the same frame gives a centre-half CALM 71% and a pixel count of CALM 34% vs STRESS 33%. Teal leads where the facing puts it, but not the whole frame decisively, and the ledger should say so.

This is far less than the base, which re-revealed on every mutation, scroll or size tick, so nothing is required. To make it strictly once per caption, keep an always-exposed visually hidden copy of the text in the live root and mark the visual band aria-hidden.

The ad-hoc tour checker (not in CI, last used in report 261103-univvis) waits on locator('[aria-live="polite"]').filter({hasText}).waitFor(). Playwright's default state is 'visible', and a zero-size live root never becomes visible, so caption() would time out now. Point it at '[data-sequence-caption-band]' or '[aria-live="polite"] p', or wait with state 'attached'. Its other '[aria-live="polite"] p' locators still work.

review.summary:
T263 meets its acceptance. One `captionHeld = advancePending || sweeping` now drives both the existing dwell pause and the shown caption, so the two cannot disagree.

The hold cannot outlive the advance. `pending` clears on the overlay's `take()` as soon as its machine is idle, and both universe pages always mount the overlay. `sampledTime` clears through `sweep.end()` when the sweep finishes or on unmount mid-sweep. Under reduced motion the sweep never begins and `onDone` fires at once. An empty interval never announces and releases at once. A failed launch announces nothing and reports no `launch-succeeded`. So every path that held the dwell before releases the caption with it, and nothing new can stick.

There is no early flash. The write flow calls `announceAdvance` before `LAUNCH_OK`, and the report the host turns into step 6 arrives one commit later. That is the same effect flush that calls `sweep.begin()`, so step 6 renders already held.

The ONB-20 channel is untouched (`takeOnboardingReport` and `onboardingReportAction` are unchanged), so a held `launch-succeeded` still advances on the step that awaits it. The demo does not use `useUniverseScreen` (only the web and mobile UniversePage do), so it is unaffected. Mobile `pointerEvents="box-none"` on `topRight` is correct: the column's empty area passes touches through while its children stay hittable. It is recorded as device-unverified.

The new tests import `tourCaptionHeld` and `shownTourCaption`, which the base lacks, so they fail there. The probe shots show no caption at t02 while the clock rolls (2026-11-07), then the caption at t03 with the clock on 11-09 and the new star in place.

Ran: `packages/universe` `use-universe-screen.test.ts` 8/8, `apps/web` `tsc -b` clean, `apps/mobile` `tsc --noEmit` clean.
